# vpsie_bare_metal_plans (Data Source)

Lists the bare-metal hardware plans a datacenter offers. A datacenter that sells no bare metal returns an empty list.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "vpsie_bare_metal_plans" "example" {
  dc_identifier = "dc-identifier"
  min_ram_gb    = 64
  min_disk_gb   = 1000
  gpu           = false
}

output "in_stock_plans" {
  value = [for p in data.vpsie_bare_metal_plans.example.plans : p.name if p.available_servers > 0]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `dc_identifier` (String) Identifier of the datacenter.

### Optional

- `gpu` (Boolean) `true` for plans with GPUs only, `false` for plans without.
- `min_disk_gb` (Number) Only plans with at least this much disk, in GB.
- `min_ram_gb` (Number) Only plans with at least this much RAM, in GB.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The datacenter identifier.
- `plans` (Attributes List) The matching plans. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--plans))

<a id="nestedatt--plans"></a>
### Nested Schema for `plans`

Read-Only:

- `available_servers` (Number) Servers in stock for the plan.
- `contract_terms` (List of String) Billing terms the plan can be ordered on (`hourly`, `monthly`).
- `cpu_count` (Number) Number of CPU cores.
- `currency` (String) Currency of the price.
- `delivery` (String) `instant` (in stock) or `build_to_order`.
- `delivery_hours` (Number) Hours a build-to-order server takes to deliver.
- `disk_gb` (Number) Total disk in GB.
- `disk_type_summary` (String) Disk layout, for example `2 x 960 GB NVMe`.
- `gpu_count` (Number) Number of GPUs.
- `gpu_memory_gb` (Number) Memory per GPU in GB.
- `gpu_model` (String) GPU model, empty without GPUs.
- `identifier` (String) Plan identifier, for `vpsie_bare_metal.plan_identifier`.
- `link_speed_options` (List of Number) Uplink speeds in Mbit/s the plan can be ordered with.
- `name` (String) Plan name.
- `price` (String) Monthly price, as a decimal string.
- `processor_model` (String) Processor model.
- `ram_gb` (Number) RAM in GB.
- `setup_fee` (String) One-time setup fee, as a decimal string.
